title: H-prime Cheon BSGS: Fraction-exact coverage census, rule-of-three key rate, derived gap tail

claims.statement: For the protected BLS12-381 G1 auxiliary-powers inputs T=A_1=[s]P0 and A_d=[s^d mod r]P0 with d=2^20, uniform nonzero s, and every integer n>=2^20, Cheon's reduction gives v=s^d mod r in H={x:x^m=1}, the subgroup of d-th powers of prime order m=(r-1)/d (235 bits, v2(r-1)=32, 6|m so mu6 is inside H), and s is determined by v up to the d roots s*zeta^j. The attack walks N=65196422678611466571411401699906505=2^115.6503 elements per side on scalars x=a*w, y=a'*w' with a,a' H-primes (q^m=1 mod r) in disjoint pools inside (2^77,2^97) and w,w' H-primes from the shared walk list of the first 2^50 H-primes above 2^39; the list's own density law 1/(d ln q) makes its top 2^76.1 and every even gap <=2^33, read through a 2^32-entry table, so x=a*w<2^174<r lies in H with no character table and every chain starts above the gap bound. Each step is one batched incomplete affine addition priced at the track's C=2000 reference unit plus 238 charged overhead instructions: the itemised rows sum to 198 and are stressed by exactly 6/5, so c=2238/2000=1119/1000. Every row is a complete instruction list, including the previously omitted ones: the scatter counter read/decrement/store, the counting-loop key load (4 per record per pass, so a pass is 25 not 21), the group_runs scan as an explicit ten-instruction op list, a two-limb gap load, and routing as 3 record copies plus a final store (the last hop's store IS the placement). Matching routes the top 85 key bits in 4 hops, orders 63 further bits with 3 LSD counting-sort passes of 21-bit digits, and the group scan compares all four 56-bit limbs, so a match is a full 224-bit key equality (the 76 bits no pass orders are compared, not assumed sorted); the key is the even one of y,p-y truncated to 224 bits, so one cross-side record pair tests the six points [u]X, u in {+-1,+-omega,+-omega^2}. Coverage is success=E[C_distinct]/m with C_distinct the cardinality of the K_cand=6N^2 candidate occurrences v=x/(u x'); under H3occ (candidate multiset ~ K_cand uniform draws into m bins) success=1-exp(-K), K=6N^2/m=51/100, an occupancy form that already contains random repetition. The coverage model's error is MEASURED as exact Fractions, never as rounded strings: six censuses over two toy fields (r=8391553, r=33555073) and d in {8,16,64}, each at the production design point K_cand 0.495-0.515, enumerate the whole candidate set and count its exact cardinality D. Row A, the per-cell excess of the raw shortfall over the counted diagonal, (pred-D-diag)/m, has exact maximum 283/174824=0.0016187800 (r=8391553,d=16; the raw fraction 849/524472=0.0016187707 and its declared ceiling is 0.00161878, so the charge exceeds the raw value); row B, the residual after removing the diagonal inside the prediction, (pred_eff-D)/m, has exact maximum 1421/262236=0.0054187900 (raw 2842/524472=0.0054187690, charged ceiling 0.00541879). Both cells are asserted Cell-by-cell against the DECLARED bound as Fractions built from the raw integer counts in the evidence JSON, and the two rows are charged as Fractions: 0.00703757 in total. The key-collision rate is NOT claimed at 2^-120 or any measured uniformity: the measured zero full-key collisions among 1999079 prefix-equal pairs at 126-bit key width gives only the rule-of-three bound 3/1999079=2^-19.35 per compared pair, and that is the rate charged. With 2^83.30 in-group pairs there are 2^63.95 expected false keys, each verified by one full scalar multiplication, against a 2^88 verification cap (Markov 2^-24.05, charged 2^-24); the ledger closes at ANY rate at or below 2^-30 (2^53.30 false keys, Markov 2^-34.70) and in fact at any rate at or below 2^-4.0, and the charged 2^-19.35 is a rate the measurement actually supports. The deeper 24/32/48/64-bit residual probes carry expected collision counts 2^-3.1/2^-11.1/2^-27.1/2^-43.1 in this many pairs, so their zero counts are uninformative and no deeper uniformity is claimed; the 8-16 bit deviation ratios 0.987/0.986/1.082 are what the 1.7 factor is taken from, and the transfer to 224-bit keys is labelled a modelling premise (H3dev), not a rate. The walk-list gap tail is DERIVED, not compared: H-primes have density 1/(d ln q) because a random residue is an m-th power with probability exactly 1/d and primality costs 1/ln q, so mean gap mu=d ln q<=d ln(2^97.1)=2^26.07 over the list, and for geometric gaps P(max gap over 2^50 > G)<=2^50 exp(-G/mu)=2^-125.6 at the charged G=2^33 (G that would give exactly 2^-40 is 2^32.04); the same law is checked against the toy's 1199 consecutive H-prime gaps (mean 468.30 against 16*ln(2^51)=565, chi-square fitted to the geometric model, tail below the model at every threshold), so the toy data validate the law and the production transfer is analytic. Node occupancy is Chernoff-charged 2^-40 at 6.31x mean. Coverage is K=51/100, so success after every debit is 0.39950-0.00703757-0.000601-2^-24-2^-40-2^-50=0.391865>=39/100. Work is 2*N*2238 instructions for the two walks plus chain tables, per-node fixed work, H-prime supply, the derived walk list, run-pair cap, 2^88 verification cap, root extraction and the 2^20-candidate T-scan; an independent order audit on a small j=0 fixture verifies [n]P=O for a prime n with n|#E by brute-force point counting, and no partG point is claimed to have order equal to its scalar modulus. Total W=2^116.812976 units of 2000 instructions < claim 116.8132 < live gate 116.8271. Peak memory 2^125.1 B, no advice, preprocessing inside the total; toy.py recovers s end to end from one secret 12/200 against the enumerated 0.059317 with 0 false positives and both checks ([s]P0=T, s^d=z) passing.
